video.title: Debugging ML Code in Dev and Production with VS Code
video.rationale: Covers: topic ✓ (0:44–2:14), CO3.LO3 ✓ (6:33–7:55) [from transcript] · Amrutha Patil · tier 4 · 7:57 · 10 views · captions
video.description:
What it covers
1. Two kinds of ML bugs
2. Setting up the debugger
3. Six VS Code tools: breakpoints, pausing automatically when an error is raised, the Variables and Call Stack panels, the Debug Console, Data Wrangler and stepping.
4. Practical example: a churn model that crashes at model.fit. 
5. Silent bugs: real training output showing overfitting and the best stopping point, plus checking feature importance for leakage and checking class balance.

review.review: Excellent walkthrough of debugging in dev versus production, structured logs, and reproducing failures safely. Highly relevant for practical log analysis.
issues: focused on ML code specifically rather than general software factory pipelines

video.title: 10 Ways to Debug Production Issues Every Developer Should Know
video.rationale: Covers: topic ✓, CO3.LO3 ✓ [from title/description only] · CodeCrack · tier 4 · 0:12 · 330 views

findings.message: coverage judged from the metadata only (no transcript or text)

video.description:
Production bugs don't come with a debugger.

Here are 10 ways real production incidents get investigated:
1. Correlation IDs
2. Distributed Tracing
3. Feature Flag Rollback
4. Canary Analysis
5. Replay Traffic
6. Heap Dumps
7. Chaos Testing
8. Synthetic Monitoring
9. Error Budgets
10. Postmortems

Correlation IDs let you follow one request across multiple services and logs.
Distributed tracing shows where time was actually spent across the entire request path.
Feature flag rollback can disable a newly introduced behavior without waiting for a full deployment.
Canary analysis compares a new version against the existing one before the change reaches everyone.
Replay traffic lets engineers repr

review.review: Great quick reference covering 10 production debugging techniques like correlation IDs and distributed tracing. Useful for modern backend workflows.
